names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 decembrie, «Sfântul Ierarh Alexandru, Arhiepiscopul Ierusalimului», with the rank word and the see left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιος Αλέξανδρος Ιερομάρτυρας Αρχιεπίσκοπος Ιεροσολύμων», with the rank and the see left off.

The nominative the day page's own `/name/` link carries in its `title`, «Святитель Александр Иерусалимский, патриарх, сщмч.», with «Святитель» and the two trailing rank words left off — `hieromartyr` is already in this folder's `types` and the see is in `office`. The calendar's own title calls him patriarch while its day line calls him «еп.», bishop, and the life page is headed «епископ Иерусалимский» and sub-headed «патриарх Иерусалимский»; the folder's existing `archbishop` was left as it stood and neither of the calendar's two words was written into `types`. The day's own line declines him «Сщмч. Александра , еп. Иерусалимского (ок. 213-250).» `fk.mjs` on «Александр Иерусалимский» returned NONE before the write, in a corpus holding some dozens of folders of the bare forename.

floruit.note: Охридски пролог за 12. децембар ст. ст.: „Био најпре епископом кападокијским. Но у време гоњења Северова 203. године бачен у тамницу и прогнан.“ — he was first bishop of Cappadocia, and in the persecution of Severus in 203 he was thrown into prison and exiled. THE 203 IS A YEAR NO OTHER SOURCE IN THIS FOLDER GAVE, and the bounds here run from it to the year of his death, which doxologia.ro and this book both put at 251. Nothing between the two bounds is claimed, and no year of birth was reckoned from either.

death.note: doxologia.ro: «Istovit de pe urma suferințelor, moare în închisoare în anul 251»; the same page dates the persecution «împăratul Deciu (249-251)» and says he was arrested «între anii 249 și 251». The Охридски пролог за 12. децембар ст. ст. agrees to the year: „бачен у тамницу, у којој и сконча свој земаљски живот и пређе ка Господу 251. године.“ — thrown into prison, where he ended his earthly life and went over to the Lord in 251.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 16 мая ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Александра , еп. Иерусалимского (ок. 213-250).»

attestations.note: The same man the folder already keeps: bishop first in Cappadocia, imprisoned under Severus, then co-bishop of Jerusalem with the aged Narcissus, and dead in prison under Decius. **The day is not the day the folder's other venerated row stands on.** The Serbian row is on 12 децембар ст. ст., and this page's own «Дни памяти» line gives both, «16 мая , 12 декабря» — so the two books agree on two days and the Russian keeps him principally on this one. One row per church is the schema, so the December day is recorded here and he does not render on it in this calendar. **`dates` were not touched.** The folder carries a floruit of 203–251 and a death of 251; the day line prints «(ок. 213-250)», which is a bracket on his episcopate and not on his life, and the page says he was chosen co-ruler «в 212 году» and governed the church of Jerusalem thirty-eight years — 212 and 38 reaching 250, which is the day line's second figure. 250 against the folder's 251 is one year inside a persecution both books put at 249 to 251, and nothing was moved. The day page prints no hymn for him. azbyka.ru was not read.

feast.note: His own page says he is kept on two days: «Este pomenit în Biserica Ortodoxă pe 16 mai și pe 12 decembrie ca ieromartir». The corpus keeps one feast to a church, so the day the calendar for 12 decembrie prints is the one recorded, and 16 mai is noted here.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 decembrie — «Sfântul Ierarh Alexandru, Arhiepiscopul Ierusalimului»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Αλέξανδρος Ιερομάρτυρας Αρχιεπίσκοπος Ιεροσολύμων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the pupil of Clement of Alexandria who was coadjutor and successor to Narcissus of Jerusalem and died in prison in the persecution of Decius. Its head gives «(; - 251)», the year the folder already holds. The page adds «Η μνήμη του Αγίου Αλέξανδρου επαναλαμβάνεται και την 16η Μαΐου» — a second Greek commemoration on 16 May, recorded here as a note because one attestation row per church is the schema, and the row records the day page read. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.12.2025 (12. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свештеномученик Александар, епископ јерусалимски.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. NO `sr` NAME FORM, AND THAT IS A REFUSAL ON THE 12-03 READING: stripping «Свештеномученик» (a rank) and «епископ јерусалимски» (a rank and a see, which this corpus puts in `types` and the display name) leaves the bare «Александар», which `sr-foldpred.mjs` measures at SIX other holders — and `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs` already carries a READ_FOLDS key for exactly those six, written for the Julian 3 July, whose own reading says the Prologue gives that fold no way to break. Storing the form would widen a keyed six to seven for no gain in telling him apart. `types` UNTOUCHED: «Свештеномученик» is the `hieromartyr` held, and the `archbishop` is the other calendars’ word for a see this book calls «епископ». `dates`: the `death` of 251 UNTOUCHED and AGREED — «пређе ка Господу 251. године», which is doxologia.ro’s «moare în închisoare în anul 251» — and a `floruit` ADDED whose earlier bound is this book’s own stated year: «у време гоњења Северова 203. године бачен у тамницу и прогнан», in the persecution of Severus in 203 he was thrown into prison and exiled. That is a year neither other calendar gave, and it brackets his public life with the death. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: that HE WAS FIRST BISHOP OF CAPPADOCIA before he took the throne of Jerusalem; that he FOUNDED THE FAMOUS LIBRARY OF JERUSALEM, which Eusebius used in writing his Church History; and that under Decius he was tortured in various ways and thrown to the beasts, and when he came out alive and untouched by them was thrown into prison, where he ended his earthly life. NO `locations`: Cappadocia and Jerusalem are two places and the folder has never held a coordinate. NO `related` ROW ADDED: `narcissus-of-jerusalem` was already here, and Eusebius, Severus and Decius are no folders this corpus holds. THE ROMANIAN ROW’S SECOND DAY, 16 mai, is already noted there and this book gives him no second day of its own. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
